SPHY, HYG and USHY against the ICE BofA US High Yield Index (H0A0)

ETF prices to 30 Oct 2026; NAV and index to 29 Oct 2026. FRED serves H0A0 history only from 31 Oct 2023, so index-relative statistics use 751 common trading days (01 Nov 2023 to 29 Oct 2026). Price-versus-NAV statistics use each fund's full history: SPHY from 2012, HYG from 2007, USHY from 2017.

Summary

  • SPHY's NAV total return has a daily correlation of 0.984 with H0A0, a beta of 0.95 and annualised tracking error of 0.59%. HYG's figures are 0.979, 1.10 and 0.84%; USHY's are 0.999, 1.01 and 0.11%.
  • Closing prices correlate with H0A0 at 0.78 to 0.79 on daily returns across the three funds, 0.94 weekly and 0.98 to 0.99 monthly.
  • SPHY traded at an average premium of +0.12% to NAV in the window (standard deviation 0.16%). The widest premium was +1.48% on 09 Apr 2025 and the widest discount -0.78% on 18 Dec 2024. Premium deviations have a one-day autocorrelation of 0.36 and a five-day autocorrelation of 0.09.
  • The daily correlation between SPHY's price return and NAV return was between 0.11 and 0.24 in each year from 2012 to 2017 and between 0.66 and 0.87 in each year from 2019 to 2026. It is 0.70 on the third of days with the highest NAV volatility, against 0.33 and 0.37 on the other two thirds.
  • Over the last twelve distributions SPHY paid 0.592% of spot per month (7.10% annualised) with a standard deviation of 0.010 percentage points, the smallest dispersion of the three funds. Its annualised distribution yield averages 1.04 times H0A0's effective yield (HYG 0.82, USHY 0.95).
  • Realised daily volatility is 3.19% for SPHY NAV, 3.30% for H0A0 and 4.77% for SPHY's closing price.

Funds and benchmarks

SPHY (SPDR Portfolio High Yield Bond ETF) lists the ICE BofA US High Yield Index, that is H0A0, as its benchmark; SSGA's page states that its index history before 1 April 2019 reflects a different index, the ICE BofAML US Diversified Crossover Corporate Index. USHY tracks the ICE BofA US High Yield Constrained Index, a variant of the same index family that caps issuer weights; iShares states that USHY has followed the 4pm pricing variant since 1 December 2023 (previously 3pm). HYG tracks the iBoxx USD Liquid High Yield Index, which is a different index from H0A0. The tracking statistics below therefore compare SPHY with its own benchmark and the other two funds with a related index (USHY) and a different one (HYG).

Current readings: H0A0's effective yield was 7.99% and its option-adjusted spread 3.26% on 29 Oct 2026. On 04 Sep 2026 they were 7.20% and 2.68%, and on 02 Oct 2026 8.13% and 3.10%, with the total return index falling 2.4% over those four weeks.

Correlation with H0A0

Returns are total returns with each distribution added back on its ex-date, measured on dates when both the index and the ETF have an observation. The annualised tracking error (TE) is the standard deviation of the ETF return minus the H0A0 return.

HYGprice0.7810.9430.9821.171.083.121.440.90
USHYNAV0.9991.0001.0001.011.010.110.110.11
USHYprice0.7900.9450.9821.151.102.971.460.88

NAV correlations are 0.979 to 0.999 on daily returns. USHY's NAV is almost indistinguishable from the index, as expected for a Constrained variant of H0A0. SPHY's daily beta of 0.95 lies below one, and its weekly and monthly betas are 0.98 and 1.01. HYG's beta is 1.10 daily.

The daily price correlation is close to 0.79 for all three funds even though the NAV correlations differ, and the daily tracking error of price against H0A0 is 3.0% to 3.1% for each. The gap between price and index therefore comes from the closing price of each fund, with the portfolio contributing little in comparison. Aggregating to weekly returns cuts the price tracking error to about 1.4% and monthly returns to about 0.8%.

For SPHY, about 0.25 of the previous day's price return appears in today's NAV return on top of 0.54 of today's, and the lagged term has a t-statistic of 11.8. HYG and USHY give similar coefficients. In the regression on H0A0, SPHY's NAV carries a small positive weight of 0.05 on the prior-day index return (t = 4.2), HYG a negative weight, and USHY none. These patterns are consistent with closing prices absorbing information a day before the bond valuations that feed NAV. I did not verify each provider's valuation time, so the mechanism is an inference from the lag structure.

Premium and discount to NAV

Daily NAV is published by SSGA for SPHY and by iShares for HYG and USHY, so the premium (closing price over NAV, minus one) can be tracked for every trading day since each fund's launch.

In the window the premium of all three funds is positive on average, between +0.12% and +0.16%, and its standard deviation is 0.16% to 0.18%. SPHY's premium exceeded 50bp in absolute terms on 1.1% of days, against 2.1% for HYG and 2.7% for USHY. All three reached their widest premium on 9 April 2025, the day of the tariff pause rally, with SPHY at +1.48%, HYG at +1.49% and USHY at +1.60%. The premium decays quickly: SPHY's autocorrelation is 0.36 at one day, 0.09 at five days and 0.02 at 21 days.

The full history shows larger excursions. SPHY's premium reached +4.48% on 09 Apr 2020 and -2.95% on 09 Mar 2020, with a one-day autocorrelation of 0.63 and a 21-day autocorrelation of 0.44. HYG's premium reached +12.76% on 05 Jan 2009 and -8.40% on 17 Sep 2008. These extremes appear in both the published NAV and the closing price series, and I did not check them against a third source.

Within the window the premium widens with the level of H0A0's spread. SPHY's premium has a standard deviation of 0.11% in the tightest third of OAS days (2.59% to 2.86%) and 0.22% in the widest third (3.18% to 4.61%).

For SPHY the price-to-NAV correlation was between 0.11 and 0.24 in each year from 2012 to 2017, rose to 0.42 in 2018 and 0.66 in 2019, and has stayed between 0.69 and 0.87 since 2020. The rolling 60-day correlation ranged from -0.11 (Jul 2014) to 0.94 (Sep 2026); it was below 0.5 on 44% of days and below zero on 3.7%. HYG's rolling correlation was below zero on 0.5% of days (low -0.15 in Jun 2009) and USHY's never fell below 0.44.

The premium-change correlation is negative for SPHY in every year from 2012 to 2018 (between -0.34 and -0.12, with -0.34 in 2015 the most negative) and positive from 2020 onward (between 0.16 and 0.25). Distributions as a share of spot

Each fund pays twelve distributions a year; the late-December payment replaces January's. The yield per distribution is the amount divided by the last close before the ex-date, and the annualised figure multiplies it by twelve. SPHY's distribution amounts come from Yahoo Finance and are rounded to three decimals, which adds a sampling noise of roughly 0.001 percentage points to its percentage figures, small against the dispersion reported.

Against H0A0's effective yield, sampled on each ex-date, SPHY's annualised distribution yield has a level correlation of 0.69 and a mean ratio of 1.04 (standard deviation 0.055). HYG's correlation is 0.26 with a ratio of 0.82, and USHY's 0.14 with 0.95. Volatility

Volatility figures are annualised standard deviations of daily or weekly total returns over the 751-day window. Weekly returns use Friday-to-Friday levels.

On daily returns the three NAVs have volatilities of 3.19% (SPHY), 3.72% (HYG) and 3.32% (USHY) against 3.30% for H0A0, and the closing prices 4.77%, 4.92% and 4.78%. H0A0 has a first-order daily autocorrelation of 0.26, so its weekly volatility of 3.71% is above the daily figure. The closing price has a first-order autocorrelation of -0.05 for SPHY, so premium noise that reverses within days adds to daily variance and washes out at longer horizons; at weekly frequency SPHY's price volatility is 4.27% against 3.65% for NAV.

Over the window H0A0's option-adjusted spread averaged 3.07% with a standard deviation of 0.36%, ranging from 2.59% (22 Jan 2025) to 4.61% (07 Apr 2025). Its effective yield averaged 7.19% (standard deviation 0.52%, range 6.39% to 9.38%). Daily changes have a standard deviation of 7.0bp for the spread and 7.4bp for the yield. The worst daily index returns were on 4 April 2025 (-1.20%), 3 April 2025 (-1.13%) and 7 April 2025 (-0.83%).

Data and method

  • H0A0 total return index, option-adjusted spread and effective yield: FRED series BAMLHYH0A0HYM2TRIV, BAMLH0A0HYM2 and BAMLH0A0HYM2EY, ICE data. FRED provides about three years of history, which limits every index-relative statistic. The pricing time of the ICE standard variant changed on 1 December 2023 according to iShares; I made no adjustment for it, which at most affects the first month.
  • SPHY NAV and shares outstanding: SSGA NAV history; fund details on the SSGA SPHY page. HYG and USHY NAV and distributions: the iShares fund download for HYG and USHY. Closing prices and SPHY distributions: Yahoo Finance via yfinance, unadjusted close.
  • iShares and Yahoo distribution amounts agree to within 0.0006 per share for HYG and USHY. A duplicate SPHY distribution listed on consecutive days in May 2016 was removed. The late-October 2026 NAV for SPHY is missing for 30 October, so SPHY statistics end on 29 October.
  • Correlations of returns across index and ETF use total-return levels on common dates, because the FRED file includes weekends and bond-market holidays on which the ETFs do not trade. Price-versus-NAV statistics use each ETF's own trading days and exclude non-trading NAV strikes such as Good Friday 2024.
  • Tercile regimes are formed by sorting days on the trailing 21-day NAV volatility (full history) or on the index OAS level (window). Standard errors in the NAV regressions are Newey-West with five lags. Episode dates are chosen by hand and are listed in the table.
  • Past statistics describe this sample. Three years of index history is short for regime comparisons: the window contains one stress episode (April 2025) and a smaller sell-off in September and October 2026. This report is analysis for internal discussion and is not investment advice.
